runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with a win over 7f on Good in recent form and strong similar-going record (5/5); the Kubler yard is ticking along at 2/9 over 14 days, and at OR 75 this horse has the class to dictate solo — though STYLE_FIT of 0.90 flags it is nominally listed as prominent rather than lead, so watch for whether it truly commits to the front from the off.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a horse fresh off a 34-day break that won over 7f on Soft and placed on Good, and whose prominent style makes it a natural beneficiary of a solo-led moderate gallop; the Kent yard is 1/7 in the 14-day window, and headgear (p) may sharpen its early intent — though the step back up to a mile on Good to Firm after a recent quiet run at 7f is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Mr Nugget
runners_data.note: Simcock's five-year-old arrives 121 days off the track with a strong placed and winning record at 8f on Tapeta, though this switch to turf and Good to Firm represents an unknown surface factor; the prominent style suits the anticipated race shape, and OR 73 gives it a live chance if the turf form translates — the yard is 0/13 over 14 days, which is a mild negative flag.

runners_data.name: War Chant
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes the mount on a horse returning from 189 days off, whose true character is front-running or prominent — it's been placed onto the map in midfield solely because the field is congested near the pace; OR 72 and recent Tapeta form over 10f suggest stamina is not an issue at a mile, but the lengthy absence and likely awkward position make its chance structurally dependent on a scenario it may struggle to create.

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: Ghiani partners a four-year-old wearing headgear (t) who has placed twice in recent starts over 7-8f and is just 14 days between runs; a genuine hold-up horse whose 5/14 similar-going record is modest, and at Yarmouth's flat mile a steady pace set by Distinct Spirit is the biggest threat to its late-running style — needs things to set up ideally.

runners_data.name: Rogue Dynasty
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides a lightly-weighted hold-up type (OR 68) with a solid recent form string of placed efforts including a win, and a 7/14 record on similar going is the best of the hold-up trio; James Owen's barn is notably active (11/48 over 14 days) and headgear (p) suggests freshness, but the race shape as anticipated offers limited room for a true closer to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes the ride on a hold-up specialist — its genuine rear-rank style means it has been redistributed to a midfield slot on the map as the field is not short of hold-up types; Dwyer sends it out just 1/4 in the recent 14-day window, the horse has placed twice on Good at 8f, and headgear (t) is retained, but STYLE_FIT of 0.90 signals its natural running position may simply not be accessible in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Distinct Spirit is the lone confirmed front runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat, undemanding mile. Drifts Away and Mr Nugget are both prominent types who will track closely, creating a small cluster near the front, but none are likely to force a truly contested early pace that would unsettle Distinct Spirit's rhythm. The hold-up trio of Panelli, Rogue Dynasty, and Man Of Desert will be anchored at the rear, requiring a strong enough gallop to close on — which a solo, unchallenged front runner rarely produces. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the leader, as the likely steady-to-moderate pace will leave little ground to make up from off it; War Chant and Man Of Desert, genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively, have been pushed back on the map because the field contains more pace-seeking runners than can all secure their natural position, with Distinct Spirit and Drifts Away most likely to control the front end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Distinct Spirit Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit gets a clean break and dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Distinct Spirit sets a rhythm that suits neither a true sprint finish nor a deep stamina test, with the race run at a pace that flatters the leader and nearby trackers; Drifts Away and Mr Nugget, sitting handily off the pace, are ideally positioned to capitalise if the front runner ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit fades in the final furlong and a close-up tracker produces a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: The steady early gallop means those tracking within two lengths of the leader carry full momentum into the straight and simply have to pick up; Mr Nugget's course-and-distance profile and Drifts Away's natural front-rank style make them the likeliest beneficiaries of any slight fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and opens enough of a gap for the rear-rank closers to find meaningful late momentum.
scenarios.body: Panelli and Rogue Dynasty, the most consistent hold-up performers in this field, would need a genuinely honest gallop to close ground from last to first on a flat Yarmouth straight; given the redistribution of War Chant and Man Of Desert away from their natural positions, the true hold-up contingent is thin and this shape is the least structurally supported.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit dramatically eases down or the field bunches and the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A sudden slowdown would scramble positions and open the race to any horse with a sharp turn of foot regardless of style; in this low-probability shape, Rogue Dynasty's consistent placing form and Panelli's recent placed efforts at similar trips give them an outside chance of grabbing a position advantage at the key moment.

watchPoints.text: Distinct Spirit jumps cleanly — if it misses the break even slightly, the prominent pair Drifts Away and Mr Nugget could barge into an unplanned lead and fundamentally alter the pace shape.

War Chant's 189-day absence combined with its natural prominent tendency means it could race keenly once the gates open and inject unexpected pace into the early exchanges, compressing the lead and tightening the race for Distinct Spirit.

Panelli and Rogue Dynasty — the two most genuine hold-up types — are both wearing headgear and may be ridden more prominently than their styles suggest if connections fear a slow tempo; watch in-running to see whether either tracks up early.

The Good to Firm going (confirmed by the going report for this race) is the fastest surface in the card and will encourage a clean, front-end display — any horse with a concern on quick ground should be noted, particularly Man Of Desert whose recent wins have come on Good rather than firmer.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Starfinch
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Harry Eustace whose recent form includes a win at Southgate but alarming efforts of 14th and 9th on Good ground; 82 days off the track is a notable concern and her similar-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 4 runs makes this a tough ask from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Caviar Cowboy
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's consistent three-year-old has found his form with three wins and places from his last five over this 7f course-and-distance trip at Southgate on Standard; Daniel Muscutt takes the ride and he handles the Good to Firm well, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is operating at the front here and this is genuinely his natural role — no discount warranted.|

runners_data.name: Three Non Blondes
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners Hayley Turner's filly who returned to form with a win at Southgate 13 days ago over 7f on Standard, and her two runs at Yarmouth on Good ground place her 2/6 with one placing — reasonable course-and-going profile; she is a natural prominent racer and has a realistic chance of sitting the prime tracking position behind the leader.|

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas's well-credentialled three-year-old carries a strong similar-going record (6 runs, 2 wins, 5 places on Good) and Tom Marquand is an elite booking, but he is a genuine prominent type whose natural position is compromised by the presence of Caviar Cowboy and Three Non Blondes — he may be forced to race slightly further back than ideal, which the STYLE_FIT flag reflects.|

races.paceDynamic: Caviar Cowboy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and should secure an uncontested lead from the gates on the Good to Firm turf at Yarmouth's flat seven furlongs, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop. Three Non Blondes and Hardy's Hero are genuine prominent types who want to race close to the pace but cannot both occupy that space behind Caviar Cowboy, meaning one will likely be nudged wider or forced to settle slightly further back than ideal — Hardy's Hero is the more likely to be displaced given Three Non Blondes' more recent race fitness. Starfinch operates from hold-up, meaning this modest, controlled tempo is a potential concern for a horse that needs others to do the donkey work. With Caviar Cowboy dictating a fair but unrushed pace and no genuine pressure from behind, this race shape strongly favours the horse able to track the leader and produce a clean, sustained finish — prominent types who can sit second and pounce from the furlong-pole hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caviar Cowboy Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Caviar Cowboy dictates an uncontested, controlled gallop and has enough in reserve to quicken off a genuine pace from the front.
scenarios.body: Caviar Cowboy, rated OR 85 and in career-best form with three consecutive placed runs including a win over this exact course and trip, sets fractions that suit his own rhythm and is never headed; with no horse applying serious pressure, he could simply sustain his effort to the line on ground he handles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Caviar Cowboy's pace proves just slightly too strong for him to maintain and a prominent tracker swoops past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Three Non Blondes or Hardy's Hero, racing close to the pace in second or third, inherit the lead as Caviar Cowboy weakens; the Good to Firm ground and seven-furlong trip on this flat track rewards a horse that has been saving energy behind the leader through the middle stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow throughout that the field bunches and Starfinch can produce a late burst without needing genuine pace-generated gaps.
scenarios.body: Starfinch gets a dream scenario where a compressed field allows her to run through the pack without needing a true end-to-end gallop, but her recent form (14th and 6th on similar going) and only 2 runs from 4 in similar conditions placing well makes this a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Field Splits
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position causes a messy pace scenario with multiple horses refusing to settle and the race becomes ragged.
scenarios.body: In a small field of four, any positional dispute between Three Non Blondes and Hardy's Hero for the prime tracking spot behind Caviar Cowboy could disrupt rhythm for all, opening a race that rewards whoever finds the cleanest passage; this scenario is unlikely given the limited pace competition but possible if tactics unravel.

watchPoints.text: Watch Caviar Cowboy's opening quarter-mile — if he slips the field uncontested through the first two furlongs on this flat Yarmouth track he could prove very hard to reel in at any price.

Monitor the early battle for the tracking position between Three Non Blondes and Hardy's Hero — one will have to concede ground and the loser may be left in an unnatural hold-up position that damages their chance.
Starfinch's 82-day absence combined with a 0-from-4 record on similar Good ground makes her a significant pace-dependent risk — if Caviar Cowboy dictates a steady tempo she may never get competitive.

Going listed as Good to Firm for this race at Yarmouth — all four runners are tagged OK for going, but the fast surface slightly increases the premium on prominent positioning and early foot rather than a late run from off the pace.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old has one course-and-distance win at 7f Yarmouth on Good ground and is the uncontested pace setter here, though his form string (79-150) shows inconsistency and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests his chance should be tempered if this pace map demands he sustain an atypical role throughout.

runners_data.name: Mercury Day
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been campaigned predominantly at 6f recently, stepping back to 7f for Conrad Allen whose 0/2 14-day record offers no yard confidence; a genuine hold-up horse who needs a faster tempo than this shape is likely to generate to be seen at best.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's five-year-old has a solid 7f record including a win and a second on Good ground at this trip, and De Sousa's tactical experience from a prominent pitch makes him the most dangerous challenger to the leader if the gallop remains modest into the straight.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: James Owen's four-year-old has been remarkably consistent — five runner-up or better finishes from six starts on Good ground at 7f — and Harry Davies keeps it simple from a hold-up position, though the absence of a win (0W5P on similar going) raises a valid question about whether this horse can convert when the moment arrives.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams fits the visor again on this five-year-old who has been running in much larger fields at 7-8f on Good and posting deeply unimpressive figures (0W0P similar going, 11th last time at Yarmouth); though natural running style is hold-up, the redistribution to midfield on the map does not reflect where this horse will settle — expect it near the rear with very little to recommend it tactically.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: David Simcock's lightly-raced four-year-old steps down in trip from 8f back to 7f where he has a Catterick win, and the OR=59 opens handicap room, but a 0/13 trainer 14-day strike rate and the true hold-up style being squeezed out of a rear position in this pace shape makes impact difficult to envision without significant improvement on recent efforts.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Ubiquitous is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a six-runner field, he should stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead at a sustainable Good-to-Firm gallop over Yarmouth's straight seven furlongs. Berry Clever will press from a prominent berth under Silvestre De Sousa, but the remaining four — Mercury Day, Rogue Allegiance, North View, and Campani — are all hold-up types who will be stationed behind the pace with varying degrees of ground to make up in the straight. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses with a well-timed mid-race move, as the moderate, uncontested tempo set by Mr Ubiquitous is unlikely to stretch the field sufficiently to guarantee the lead holds, but it equally will not generate the strong pace that true closers need to pounce late. Note that the field contains more hold-up horses than can realistically deploy from their natural position — North View and Campani are both genuine rear-of-field types redistributed onto the pace map; they are the least likely to benefit from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ubiquitous Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ubiquitous bowls along at a comfortable clip and the hold-up brigade never generate a meaningful late surge.
scenarios.body: Mr Ubiquitous dictates from the front on a flat, straight track with minimal pressure, and Berry Clever, tracking closely under De Sousa, is ideally placed to quicken off the steady tempo at the two-furlong pole. Prominent-to-lead profiles benefit most when the pace is self-regulated and the straight is long enough to absorb a finishing kick without needing a strong gallop to close from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and a well-positioned hold-up type delivers a sustained late run through tired horses.
scenarios.body: Rogue Allegiance's consistent placed form at this trip and going — five top-three finishes from six runs on Good — makes her the most credible closer if the tempo quickens and creates a true test in the final two furlongs. Mercury Day would need to improve on recent efforts but has the engine to pounce if the race develops a genuine pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If Berry Clever kicks hard early in the straight and forces Mr Ubiquitous to race beyond his comfort zone, collapsing the front runner late.
scenarios.body: Berry Clever has good form at this track and trip under conditions like these, and De Sousa's tactical aggression could exploit an uncontested front runner who has a habit of finishing mid-pack in run-of-race events. A proper duel for the lead transforms this into a true test of stamina at the trip's business end, and a horse with genuine hold-up ability could then mop up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Campani, stepping back from 8f to 7f and now on more suitable faster ground, produces a sharp enough sectional to overcome the pace shape disadvantage.
scenarios.body: Campani has two wins from five runs and has demonstrated tactical versatility at 7f on a sound surface, and David Simcock's yard has shown ability to place horses when fresh enough; however, the REDISTRIBUTED tag and OR=59 off a cold 0/13 trainer strike rate makes this a low-probability outcome dependent on a sharp improvement. North View's visor and course experience offer mild upside but the deeply modest recent form and 0W0P similar-going record make a forward showing structurally unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Mr Ubiquitous sets a solo lead — watch whether Berry Clever under De Sousa actively contests the front from flag fall, because that single tactical decision reshapes the entire race.

Rogue Allegiance has finished second five times on Good ground at this trip without winning — watch whether Harry Davies slots closer to the pace than usual to avoid getting trapped in a slowly-run affair that will not suit a pure closer.

North View wears a visor and steps into a race with more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — if the early pace is slow, Chloe Lyons (7lb claim) may be forced to commit earlier than ideal, compromising any late challenge.

Going is recorded as Good-to-Firm across all Yarmouth races today despite the official card listing Good — quicker ground than anticipated will favour prominent racers and could blunt the closing kick of Mercury Day and Rogue Allegiance.

Campani's OR=59 gives David Simcock's runner a significant weight pull of 13-15lbs over the top weights — watch in-running position early, as any forward move in the market at short odds would signal stable confidence that the yard believes the weight advantage overrides the tactical shape disadvantage.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Maith Mar Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with three recent runs around 10f on Good and Soft, including a third last time; the step up to 1m3½f on Good to Firm is an interesting stamina test, and Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim could be decisive in a close sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Gretna Dreams
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good going but has finished 7th twice and bolted last time out; Marco Ghiani takes the ride for Stuart Williams, whose T14 strike rate is active at 3/24, though the horse's true station is at the back of the field and it will not easily find that position here.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this three-year-old for Michael Bell, who has returned 1/21 in the last fortnight; form has been a steady 6-4-8-4 without threatening, and with no previous form beyond 10f the step to 1m3½f on quick ground introduces an untested stamina element.

runners_data.name: Caraway
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good recently and boasts the most relevant trip and going profile in this field; Tom Marquand is a strong tactical rider who may push Caraway forward to fill the pace vacuum, and despite being a natural hold-up type his best form has come when in closer contact with the pace.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a lengthy recent run of out-of-the-frame finishes, including five consecutive runs failing to make the first four; headgear (p) noted, and while John Egan is an experienced handler of hold-up types, George Margarson's T14 of 0/8 offers little encouragement despite the horse having placed form at this trip in the past.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up profile, nobody wants to go forward and this 1m3½f handicap at Yarmouth faces a genuine vacuum at the head of affairs — the field will drift into a crawl before someone is forced to make use of the Good to Firm ground earlier than they would prefer. The likely outcome is a slow-run, bunched race that detonates into a sprint finish from around the two-furlong pole, favouring those with the sharpest turn of foot over genuine stamina. Caraway, Gretna Dreams, and Twilight Guest are all natural hold-up horses mapped into midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning none will truly settle where they want and positional friction is probable throughout. This race shape, dominated by a false-pace sprint finish, squarely favours the horse with the highest cruising speed and best finishing kick — a progressive, well-handled type with strong form over this sort of trip on Good ground, regardless of nominal running style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If no runner forces the pace and the field drifts into a crawl before a furious sprint over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With Good to Firm ground rewarding acceleration, the horse who can quicken most sharply from a compressed group will dictate the result; this suits a progressive type with a high RPR and strong recent form at the trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Caraway Dictates Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Marquand decides to push Caraway forward from his natural hold-up role to control an otherwise leaderless field.
scenarios.body: Caraway's recent win over 12f on Good and strong Haggas yard form makes him dangerous if allowed a soft lead; dictating a moderate gallop then quickening from the front would play to his trip experience.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suit Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If one runner is sent forward aggressively early, setting a searching gallop that stretches the field and tests stamina.
scenarios.body: A genuinely-run race over 1m3½f on quick ground would expose any stamina weakness, benefiting the horse with the deepest staying pedigree and most consistent form at this trip and beyond.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race is truly falsely run and a lower-rated runner catches the fancied horses flat-footed at a decisive moment.
scenarios.body: Twilight Guest or Gretna Dreams, both with previous winning form at this trip, could capitalise on a muddling race where positioning luck outweighs class; both have each-way claims if the sprint develops close to their true finishing position.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Tom Marquand elects to push Caraway forward from the outset — if he moves to fill the pace vacuum, Caraway becomes a very different proposition and could steal a march on the entire field.
Monitor the early stride of Gretna Dreams; the horse bolted on its last run and any sign of John Egan unable to settle it cleanly in a field with no natural leader could compromise its race entirely.

With five hold-up horses and no confirmed front-runner, watch for significant positional crowding on the early bends as multiple riders simultaneously decide they must take a more forward berth than planned.

Maith Mar Or's claim rider Olivia Tubb (5lb) could prove significant — in a tight sprint finish over the final two furlongs the weight advantage may tip a photo in a race where little separates the principals on ratings.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chasing Gold
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Michael Keady whose best recent effort was a win over 6f on soft; Good to Firm going is fine (going=OK) but its sim-going record shows just one placing from 15 in similar conditions, and 31 days since last run is a modest freshness angle — Daniel Muscutt has to find a gap from the back in what may be a compressed finish.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this 6yo who holds a strong piece of course form (2nd/6f Good) from its best profile; carries a visor and is a genuine rear-of-field operator who has been pushed into a midfield slot because the field cannot sustain so many closers — the style compromise makes it harder to land in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: One For Harvey
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's 4yo returns after a 287-day absence, which is a major freshness flag in a competitive sprint handicap; a hold-up type by nature whose recent form on soft and standard ground has produced little, and the long layoff combined with the style fit discount (0.91) makes this a significant query on both counts.

runners_data.name: Havana Jag
runners_data.note: The only runner with an undefined pace style, whose recent form figures (2nd/5f Good, 4th/6f Good) show consistent proximity to the pace; Kaiya Fraser rides in what is a wide-open pace scenario and Havana Jag is the most natural candidate to drift into a prominent forward position — its consistent form at this course and over this sort of ground is a key positive.

runners_data.name: Ballsgrove Boy
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's gelding is back after 271 days off and has a bleak sim-going record (1 placing from 15 in similar conditions) — the layoff alone is a serious concern, and the horse's natural rear-tracking style has been pushed into midfield simply because the race is overloaded with hold-up types, not because it wants to be there.

runners_data.name: Charging Bull
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and a tongue-tie (hg:ht) and has shown a bit of form with a 2nd on soft over 5f, but its sim-going record in similar conditions (1 placing from 12) and its redistributed position (true hold-up mapped forward by field composition) both work against it; Harry Davies rides for the Keady yard who are 0/3 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games
runners_data.note: George Boughey sends this 3yo out in excellent in-form trim (5 wins from 20 in 14 days) and the tongue-tie is applied for the first time since earlier runs; it has a placing at 6f on Good ground in its history (2nd/6f Good) and Billy Loughnane is a sharp jockey for a sprint finish — this is the most interesting angle in the race from a trainer-form standpoint.

runners_data.name: Rianka
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's 3yo filly is lightly raced (only 4 runs) and wears a hood; her sim-going record is the strongest of any redistributed horse (3 placings from 4 in similar conditions), but she is a true hold-up type pressed into a midfield role by field composition, and a style fit discount of 0.90 applies — Marco Ghiani will need luck in running from an awkward position in a likely bunch finish.

races.paceDynamic: No confirmed front-runner is declared in this 8-runner 6f handicap at Yarmouth, and with the going riding Good to Firm (faster than the declared Good), the race will almost certainly compress into a sprint from the gates with no horse willing to take a clear early lead — expect a moderate pace that sets up a dash from the two-furlong pole. Havana Jag is the only runner with an undefined style tag and recent form showing prominent finishes, making it the most likely candidate to drift into a prominent early role, while Chasing Gold and Blindfold Games are the truest hold-up types who will look to pounce late. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Due Date, One For Harvey, Ballsgrove Boy, Charging Bull and Rianka all carry true hold-up profiles but have been redistributed to midfield because the race cannot accommodate that many genuine closers; Havana Jag is best placed to secure a prominent forward position, with Blindfold Games and Chasing Gold most naturally suited to the rear. This race shape — a falsely run sprint with a bunch finish — strongly favours the horse with the sharpest turn of foot from a handy position rather than those tracking from deep, giving a tactical edge to any runner who can sit just off the pace and quicken on this fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint-finish bunch race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate from flag to finish, compressing the field into a two-furlong dash with no horse gaining an early advantage
scenarios.body: Havana Jag, ideally positioned just off the pace given its recent prominent form, is best placed to quicken on the fast ground in a bunched finish; Blindfold Games, equipped with a tongue-tie and peak trainer form (Boughey 5/20 in 14 days), can deliver a well-timed late run from just off the pace

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy horse dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Jag or another runner secures an uncontested prominent position and controls the tempo through the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: With no confirmed pacesetter, a horse that jumps well and establishes a comfortable rhythm can avoid the scrimmage and simply outstay rivals who are forced wide or boxed in; Havana Jag's course-and-distance form (2nd/5f Good, 4th/6f Good) and consistent prominent finishes make it the primary beneficiary of this shape

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly fast early pace is set and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up horses to finish through beaten rivals
scenarios.body: Chasing Gold has the cleanest hold-up profile in the field and has winning form over 6f on soft ground, suggesting stamina reserves that could tell if the pace genuinely goes early; Due Date brings course form (2nd/6f Good) and Tom Marquand's experience, though its redistributed position tempers confidence in this shape delivering

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, front-runner wins
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks sharply and is allowed to coast on a loose lead unchallenged through the early stages
scenarios.body: With no natural front-runner declared, this scenario requires a tactical aberration from connections, making it the least likely outcome; should it occur, Havana Jag's undefined style and competitive early speed would make it the accidental beneficiary, though the fast ground would expose any runner trying to wire the field without the class to sustain it

watchPoints.text: Blindfold Games — George Boughey's yard is firing at a 25% strike rate over the last 14 days (5/20) and Billy Loughnane is a dangerous booking in a sprint; watch if Blindfold Games is prominent in the market or drifts, as yard form alone makes this a live runner.

One For Harvey and Ballsgrove Boy both return from layoffs exceeding 270 days — monitor market moves for either horse, as significant support without obvious explanation could signal a well-prepared return, but absent that the fitness query is real.

Havana Jag's going record (3 placings from 11 in similar conditions, no wins) suggests it hits the board without converting — watch if it breaks smartly, as from a forward position on fast ground it could prove difficult to pass but may find one too good late.

The going is being described as Good to Firm in race reports despite the official Good declaration — any horse with a going concern on fast ground should be scrutinised closely, particularly Charging Bull (soft form) and One For Harvey (recent soft/standard runs).

Rianka's sim-going record (3/4 in similar conditions) is the standout among the redistributed hold-up types — if Marco Ghiani manages to find a clear run late and the pace genuinely goes, this filly's course-going profile is worth monitoring for place purposes.

runners_data.name: Roi de Coeur
runners_data.note: Botti's three-year-old has been best at a mile on standard ground but similar-going form reads 0 wins from 4 attempts, which is a quiet flag; naturally a prominent racer, there is a mild style-fit concern here as leading may stretch the role slightly, though the lack of rivals means it won't be hard won.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Dunlop's consistent colt won two on the bounce at seven and eight furlongs on standard ground and arrives here after a 55-day absence; Tom Marquand rides for a yard in decent form (3/21 last 14 days) and the hold-up style suits a horse who needs the race to develop in front of him.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's runner arrives on the back of a win 14 days ago at this trip on good ground, and with four wins or places from five runs in similar conditions, the good-to-firm surface here is a genuine asset; Billy Loughnane tracks the pace naturally from a prominent pitch, and the trainer's tight turnaround record (1/10 last 14 days) is modest but the horse's recent form compensates.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Margarson's hold-up type has solid course-and-distance form on good ground — a win and two places from seven runs in similar conditions — but the trainer is winless from eight runners in the last fortnight, which is a quiet yard angle; J F Egan will need the pace to fold quickly with a small field, making this a difficult tactical setup for a horse who wants others to do the donkey work.

races.paceDynamic: Roi de Coeur is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner mile, and with no other natural front-runner to apply pressure, Marco Ghiani can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front. Celtic Chariot maps prominently and will likely slot in directly behind, keeping Roi de Coeur honest without forcing a truly fast gallop, while Chapman's Peak and Guest House will be held up off the pace in the latter half of the field. At Yarmouth over a mile on good-to-firm ground, a lone leader setting a sustainable gallop typically sets up a race where prominent racers can conserve energy through the middle sections and use their position to kick off the home turn. The race shape here strongly favours front-to-prominent profiles: with just four runners, the hold-up horses have limited cover and will need the pace to collapse dramatically to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur dictates a measured gallop and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough momentum in the straight to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: Roi de Coeur sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and Celtic Chariot sits close enough to pick up the pieces if Roi de Coeur tires; the short field means no pace collapse and front-to-prominent horses control the race from gate to line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a true end-to-end gallop that drains the front pair in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Chapman's Peak and Guest House, settled off the pace by Tom Marquand and J F Egan respectively, would benefit from a faster-than-expected tempo emptying the tank of the leaders; Chapman's Peak's back form of two successive wins at this course and distance makes him the primary closer threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Modest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur sets an unusually slow tempo and the race turns into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race could scramble the form book, but with only four runners it is difficult to hide, and Celtic Chariot's recent winning form and good-to-firm record gives the prominent racer an edge in a dash; Chapman's Peak's fitness after a 55-day absence becomes a bigger question in a speed duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexpected Front Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur fails to handle the going or runs below OR and fades turning for home, opening the race entirely.
scenarios.body: Guest House carries the lowest weight and has form at this course on good ground, including a win over a mile, and an uncontested breakaway scenario for another runner becomes possible; however Guest House's trainer is 0/8 over the last 14 days, making this a low-confidence outcome.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Chariot — if Billy Loughnane is able to sit a length or two off Roi de Coeur through the middle sections, he is optimally placed to strike for home at the two-furlong pole with his proven good-to-firm record and recent winning fitness.

Chapman's Peak — watch whether Tom Marquand can find any cover in a four-runner field; with so few bodies, the hold-up tactic is harder to execute and a wide, exposed run could blunt the finish that his back form promises.

Roi de Coeur — the similar-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 4 runs) is a red flag even if the controlled lead looks ideal on paper; if the horse fails to quicken when headed, it hands the race to the prominent tracker directly behind.

Guest House — lowest weight in the race (126lbs) is a marginal advantage, but the 34-day absence and a trainer cold streak (0/8 last 14 days) mean this runner needs near-perfect setup from a hold-up position in a small field to land the race.
